chapter: Buck and Bubbles: Nazarro and Bubbles
title: Demonstrating how Bubbles corrected his time step
summary: Green demonstrates the Bubbles time step and his own variation, adding visual run from behind, and the Studio Tap.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: Can you show me how he might correct you in tap? taps?
Like do something incorrectly, and then do it, say, like he told you it should be done.

Yes. Yes, I can. Now, here's a for instance of how Mr. Bubbles would correct me. (Inaudible) That was the Bubbles time step. Now I learnt myself how to do one of his steps (dancing). (Tap dancing.) (Inaudible). So he would like that. He'd say, say, 'Well that's all right. I let you get away with it that time,' he said. 'Make sure you keep it on time.'

Chuck, I notice that the sound, the rhythm sound is exactly the same, it seemed to me, but visually it was so much different. I mean, the first John Bubbles time step and then the one that you did, that you say you added a different visualness to it.

Yes. Well, a different way of doing Bubbles' rhythm, you see. It was the same step, which is time step. So you could either add a tap to the time step, or you could subtract, you see. It's just like arithmetic, see. Now, I had more visualness in the time step, because there was a sort of a run, but the run came from behind.
I noticed it that. It seemed as if you were doing that much more, your own thing, the way you used your feet. It seemed like you were doing so much more.
Then when we listened to it, the rhythm sounded more or less the same.
Would you show us again, Chuck?

Well, now, here's another for instance of Bubbles. He taught me a step like this. (Tap dancing.) See? He taught me that. He called that the Studio Tap. So now, as I said, I'd get away to myself and try to teach myself another way of doing the same step that he had taught me. So I would come back, and I came back with this here. (Tap dancing.) (Inaudible). See, I didn't want to get caught, see. He inspired me, like if someone else would attempt to teach me something, like some years later I ran into Mr. Bill Bailey, and he had envisioned a different style of tap dancing. See, like Mr. Bubbles had -- when I was telling you about the cramp, there's a cramp tap which is either the dropping of the heels or the kick cramp. Now, suppose he taught me the kick cramp, this here's the kick cramp. (Tap dancing.) That's a kick cramp.
